notes.text: This is even harder than P=\=PSPACE, not sure if it makes sense to include it by itself (on the other hand, it is probably the most important complexity-theoretic question in quantum)

notes.author: Olek Łukasiewicz
notes.text:
The linked source does not seem to treat about the real-weighted version of the problem (it rather studies the integer weights, see problem TCS-6937).

A better source might be (Chan et al., STOC 2022, doi.org/10.1145/3519935.3520032) or (R.Williams, STOC 2014, doi.org/10.1145/2591796.259181).

Also, the assumption that the truly subcubic algorithm does not exist is a weaker version of the conjecture TCS-6937 (which is more frequently linked to the problems listed below as related).

notes.author: Olek Łukasiewicz
notes.text:
The AI generated description of the problem is somewhat clumsy, I understand that it pertains to the case with polynomially bounded weights on the edges of the (directed) graph.

The source link directs to the webpage of Virginia Vassilevska Williams. I suppose that it was meant to link to the note (V.V.Williams, ICM 2018, doi.org/10.1142/9789813272880_0188) - the PDF of that note is linked directly on the aforementioned website.

notes.author: Olek Łukasiewicz
notes.text:
This problem was recently shown to be essentially equivalent to the problem TCS-6937, see (Fischer, STOC 2026, https://doi.org/10.1145/3798129.3800806).
The equivalence is conditioned on the assumption that $\omega = 2$ and a plausible conjecture from additive combinatorics.

notes.author: Olek Łukasiewicz
notes.text:
This problem is resolved, these problems are fine-grained equivalent. One direction was shown in (Bringmann et al., SODA 2018, https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611975031.77), the other in (Nogler et al., STOC 2025, https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718116).

The fine-grained complexity of the unweighted version of the problem is not yet fully known, see (Nogler et al., STOC 2025).

notes.author: Anonymous
notes.text: This is a simplification of the linear-sorting question on word-RAM. One would suspect that this could be solvable using current techniques.

notes.author: Anonymous
notes.text: This is not a yes/no question. It depends on the proof system. I think for some very limited proof systems the answer is known to be that P vs NP is independent. Perhaps one would have to specify whether it is independent of say ZFC - Zernel-Frankl theroy with axion of choice.

notes.author: Anonymous
notes.text: This is the same question as whether boolean formulas have polynomial size circuits.

notes.author: Anonymous
notes.text: This looks like a question within a reach of current techniques. Worth thinking about...

notes.text: One should check On the Complexity of Numerical Analysis by Eric Allender, Peter Bürgisser, Johan Kjeldgaard-Pedersen, and Peter Bro Miltersen

notes.text: A weaker version would be to prove that EXP has sub-exponential size circuits.

issues.title: [Problem] Streaming Euclidean MST to constant factor in space polylogarithmic in the number of points
issues.body:
<!-- atlas-problem:v1 parallel -->

### Problem statement

Goal: Design an $O(1)$-approximation insertion-only streaming algorithm for estimating the minimum spanning tree (MST) cost in the $d$-dimension Euclidean space using one pass and space $\mathrm{poly}(d\cdot \log n)$, where $n$ is the number of points in the stream. Alternatively, show that no such algorithm is possible. (The dimension $d$ can be assumed to be logarithmic in $n$.)
